career_spells.role: Assistant furniture removalist, then company truck driver
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech names Wridgways as first formal employer in 1977 and dates subsequent owner-driver transition to 1980. In 2012 Sterle instead recalled joining the TWU when he first walked through the Ansett Wridgways doors in 1976 at age 16; this conflicts with the 1977 formal-work account, so the start is not backdated. A 2024 recollection of 16 years as a furniture removalist with Ansett Wridgways appears to aggregate employee and later contractor years rather than resolve the employment boundary. Year-level boundary only; exact promotion, cessation, hours and leave unknown. Contemporary 1978 court account identifies Ansett Wridgways corporate division; private classification supported.

career_spells.employer: Own road-train and furniture-removal business; trading name unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech explicitly dates owner-driving commencement to 1980 and transition to TWU organiser to 1991, resolving age-based uncertainty. Later Hansard names Ansett Wridgways as contracting counterparty, recalls owner-driver fuel negotiations and expansion from one truck to three. Sterle's 2024 shorthand claim of 16 years as a furniture removalist with Ansett Wridgways is consistent with a long commercial relationship but does not distinguish employee service from owner-driver contracting and conflicts with the separate 1977–1980/1980–1991 phase account. Legal trading name and precise boundaries remain unknown. Extensive road travel is not a quantified or explicit full-time work history; do not infer all years full-time or add conflicting approximate narrative durations.

research_notes: Initial review2026-10-01: APH chronology, own and ALP biographies, ABC2008 transcript, government appointment, truck-industry reports and public professional results searched. First-speech PDF16August2005 returned403; no circumvention attempted.

Follow-up: named school-holiday/company employers, business trading name and registration, employee/owner transition, actual hours and breaks in trucking, cessation against1991 union appointment; historical TWU reports to delimit full-time period.

Secondary14-year owner-operator claim conflicts with own age20 start and12-year road-train narrative. Preserve official aggregate span rather than invent boundaries. Later Linfox driving visit, charity deliveries and clients such as Woodside do not establish those entities as historical employers.

Follow-up 2026-10-02: recovered full first-speech transcript via public reproduction after legacy APH failure. Resolved named first formal employer and 1980 transition; 1978 court description supports Ansett corporate structure, later personal Hansard identifies contractor relationship.

Initial note about unnamed company and age-based transition is superseded by src-9. School-holiday employer remains unknown; do not assume same Wridgways engagement. Own business trading name, full-time hours/leave and exact employment/contractor boundaries remain follow-up needs.

Searched TWU acting-secretary1998 and historic profiles: secondary repetition located but no reliable primary tenure evidence recovered, so not added as established office. Next leads: historical Wridgways employment/owner-driver records, business registration, TWU appointment/cessation reports. Modern charity and demonstration drives do not establish resumed paid full-time employment.

Follow-up 2026-10-03: additional first-person Hansard located a 1976 Ansett Wridgways/TWU recollection and a 2024 claim of 16 years as an Ansett Wridgways furniture removalist. These illuminate the long company/contractor relationship but conflict with, and do not supersede, the more specific 1977 formal-employment and 1980 owner-driver transition account. No full-time hours or exact phase boundary inferred.
